_decoded_content.title: Clarify that only known plugins are displayed in the UI, and how known plugins can be added and made UI-ready
Document how to configure Meltano UI / gunicorn for production
Stop automatically running Airflow scheduler as part of Meltano UI
_decoded_content.description:
In real-world scenarios, running it separately makes much more sense.

This tripped me up in https://gitlab.com/meltano/meltano/-/issues/2048, where a Docker container with the `meltano` entrypoint and `ui` command would not just start Meltano UI but also Airflow.

_decoded_content.title: Using UI to add extractor with related transform plugin to project fails when dbt hasn't yet been installed
_decoded_content.description:
`dbt` will automatically be installed when `meltano elt` is run with `--transform={run,only}`, but since _adding_ the transform requires `transform/dbt_project.yml` to already exist, this will fail if the [`dbt` file bundle](https://gitlab.com/meltano/files-dbt) hasn't already been added to the project, which is automatically installed along with `meltano add transformer dbt`.

Do we need to explicitly make `dbt` an install-time dependency of `transform` plugins, and ensure it and its own related plugins (i.e. the `dbt` file bundle) are installed first?

_decoded_content.title: Make it clear in UI when it's running in read-only mode
_decoded_content.description:
In read-only mode, Meltano can only be used to list existing pipelines, manually run them, and view the status and logs of the latest run.

In read-write mode, it can be used to actually manage the project: add and configure extractors, loaders, and pipelines.

Locally in development, you'd usually run it in the default read-write mode, but when deploying a [containerized Meltano project](https://meltano.com/#containerization), changes cannot be made anymore since the project has been packaged up, and the UI runs in read-only mode.

Related to https://gitlab.com/meltano/meltano/-/issues/2083

_decoded_content.title: `MELTANO_READONLY` and `MELTANO_AUTHENTICATION` interact in confusing ways
_decoded_content.description:
According to [the documentation](https://www.meltano.com/docs/environment-variables.html#authentication):

> If read-only mode is enabled (`MELTANO_READONLY=1`), authentication will only be required for write actions.

This means that authentication can't be used to protect read access. Making a meltano server publicly accessible means you expose your potentially sensitive business data to the world

_decoded_content.title: Support PORT env var as alternative to MELTANO_API_PORT
_decoded_content.description:
As @rabidaudio wrote in https://gitlab.com/meltano/meltano/-/issues/2081:

> Heroku injects a `PORT` environment variable to tell the app which port to expose. Meltano allows this but uses `MELTANO_API_PORT`.

_decoded_content.title: Let Meltano itself and Meltano UI be configured using `meltano config` and `meltano.yml` just like plugins
Have `meltano ui setup` write to `.env` instead of `ui.cfg`
_decoded_content.description:
Follow-up to https://gitlab.com/meltano/meltano/-/issues/2090

As I wrote in https://gitlab.com/meltano/meltano/-/merge_requests/1697#note_362387666:

> I'd actually prefer to move away from `ui.cfg` sooner rather than later (while continuing to support it for legacy reasons), since it doesn't have any benefits over setting these variables through `.env` or the actual environment, which is more consistent with how the rest of Meltano is configured. `meltano ui setup` could write to `.env` instead of `ui.cfg`, or just print the appropriate `export X=Y` statements with some instructions

_decoded_content.title: Allow Meltano UI logo to be changed using configuration
_decoded_content.description: This will allow consultancies to offer a whitelabel Meltano UI experience to their clients.

_decoded_content.title: Have users explicitly choose to add related transform, model, and dashboard plugins when adding an extractor through the UI
_decoded_content.description: The UI currently always runs the equivalent of `meltano add --include-related extractor <name>`, but the `--include-related` flag should be optional.

_decoded_content.title: Pipeline may get stuck in "running" mode when Meltano is upgraded and/or restarted during run
_decoded_content.description:
On a user's MeltanoData.com instance, we saw a pipeline job that had (according to the "Run Log" modal "Elapsed" time) been running for more than 4 days. 

The log showed "The log is too large to display inline. Download it below.", but the "Download Log" button was disabled because (according to Meltano) the job hadn't finished running yet, so there was no way to see from the UI whether the job was actually still running and generating output, or not.

There is also not a way to cancel or otherwise delete a pipeline that has gotten stuck, so I ended up SSH'ing in and making the change myself. This is related to https://gitlab.com/meltano/meltano/issues/1493.

_decoded_content.title: Make it easier to run Meltano UI in Docker with Airflow and Postgres containers
If start_date is in the past, scheduled Airflow DAG runs immediately after initial manual pipeline run
_decoded_content.description:
The DAG's start_date is set to the extractor's start date, while it should just be set to the timestamp of pipeline creation, so that the first schedule run won't come until the next day (or hour, etc).

Right now though, the pipeline's start_date is used in the UI where really the extractor's start_date should be used.
